sentences.text: The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 claiming compensation from the respondents due to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. Brief facts of petitioner's case is that on 03.10.2022 at about 01.45 p.m, the petitioner was traveling in KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, on Kolar-Bangalore NH Road, when the bus reached opposite to NH-75 Hotel, near Mylapura Gate Hosakote, Bangalore Rural District, the driver of said bus drove the same in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life and dashed to one Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498, which was parked on the road by its driver without any precaution, as a result of forced impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Silicon City Hospital for first aid and further shifted to Raksha Hospital, wherein, she took treatment as inpatient and wherein the duty doctors examined her clinically and radiologically, which revealed that she sustained severe neck pain and all the injuries treated with conservatively and she has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses, food, transportation, conveyance and other charges.

Due to the said accidental injuries, the petitioner completely bed ridden, cannot run, jump, cannot lift or carry any weight,
unable to sleep properly, she cannot do his activities as earlier to the accident and undergoing deep Shobha.
V vs K.S.R.T.C

2 mental shock, pain and suffering, since the injuries caused permanent in nature.
4. It is contended that, this accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773 and also due to negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D- 9498.

Hence, the Hosakote Police have registered a case against drivers of said vehicles in crime No.353/2022.
5.

It is contended that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale, healthy, aged about 33 years and she was working as House Wife and due to accidental injuries she is not able to do her job and hence she lost her earning and suffering from mental shock and agony and also facing great financial difficulties.
6.

The respondent No.1 being owner of the KSRTC Bus, Respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the Lorry, respondent No.3 being insurer of the Lorry and respondent No.4 is the insurance company of the Lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, this petition was filed against the respondents for claiming compensation.

7. In pursuance to the notice, the respondent No.1 to 4 appeared through their respective counsel and the respondent No.2 and 3 have filed joint written statement and the respondent No.1 and 4 have filed their written statements separately.

8. Brief contents of the written statement of respondent No.1 is that while admitting the ownership of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, this respondent contended that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498 as he was parked the Lorry in the middle of the road without any precautionary measurement and signals.
Hence, respondent No.2 to 4 are liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.

However,
on humanitarian ground this respondent paid the entire hospital bill amounting to Rs.31,670/- and same may be liable to be deducted and in case of holding contributory negligence on the part of the Lorry either fully or partially.
The insurer and owner of the lorry shall be directed to refund the medical expenses paid by this respondent to the petitioner to the extent of their liability.

Further, it has denied the date, place, mode of accident and nature of injuries, age, income, occupation of the petitioner, medical expenses incurred by her and disability caused to her and also contended that,
claim of the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

9. Brief contents of the written statement of respondent No.2 and 3 are that the petition filed by the petition is not maintainable neither under facts of the case nor under the question of law and it is to be dismissed in limine.

It is further contended that these respondents are the owner and driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498 who parked left side of the road and taken the required all safety and precautionary methods with due diligence, because of the negligent and rash driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, this accident was happened and the Bus suddenly came to the footpath and hit the lorry, the driver of the said bus drove the same beyond speed limits in a negligent manner without applying breaks.
The petitioner has filed this false case against the respondent No.2 and 3 with malafide intention in view of getting higher compensation Shobha.

Hence, prays to dismiss the petition against these respondents.
10. The respondent No.4 has contended in his written statement that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case and denied the entire averments of the petition.

While admitting about issuance of insurance policy in respect of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/
D-9498, this respondent restricted its liability to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that, driver of the said vehicle did not possess valid D.L. FC and permit as on the date of the accident and hence, terms and conditions of the insurance policy were violated.

It is contended that, this accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, as the driver of Lorry was parked his vehicle with all precautionary measures with signals to other vehicles.

Further these respondents denied the date, place and mode of accident, age, income and occupation of the petitioner, medical expenses incurred by her and disability caused to her and also contended that, claim of the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition with costs.

11. On basis of the pleadings and materials, this tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 03.10.2022 at about 01.45 p.m, the petitioner was traveling as a passenger in a KSRTC bus bearing Reg No.KA-57/F-3773, proceeding on NH-75, when the bus reached near Mylapura Gate Opp. to NH-75 Hotel, Hosakote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District at that time, the driver of KSRTC Bus drove the same, in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life, came at a high speed and dashed the parked Lorry bearing No.KA-16/D-9498.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. Whether order or award?
12.
In order to substantiate the case, petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11.
On the other hand, the respondents have not examined any witnesses on their sides and no documents are marked before the Court.

13. Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.
14.

REASONS 15. Issue No.1:- The petitioner filed this petition under against respondents for claiming compensation due to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

16. The petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination and in her chief affidavit she had reiterated the averments of petition and got marked 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11.

Ex.P.1 is the copy of F.I.R. Ex.P.2 is the copy of complaint, Ex.P.3 is the copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the copy of sketch, Ex.P.5 is the copy of IMV report, Ex.P.6 is the copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is the copy of charge sheet, Ex.P.8 is the discharge summary, Ex.P.9 is the lab reports, Ex.P.10 is the notarized copy of Aadhaar card and Ex.P.11 is the medical bills.

17. On perusal of Ex.P.4-spot sketch and Ex.P.7-charge sheet, it appears that, near Mylapura Gate Hosakote, opposite to NH-75 Hotel, Bangalore, the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773 drove the same, in a rash and negligent manner came at high speed and dashed to one Lorry bearing No.KA-16/D-9498, which was parked on the road by its driver without any precautionary MVC.6376/2022 measures and caused the accident.

Hence, Hosakote Police filed Charge sheet against driver of the KSRTC Bus as A.1 and driver of Lorry as A.2.
18.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.

sentences.text:
19. After careful scrutiny of Ex.P.1-F.I.R. Ex.P.2- complaint, Ex.P.3-spot mahazar, Ex.P.4-sketch,
Ex.P.5- IMV report, Ex.P.6-wound certificate and Ex.P.7-charge sheet, it appears that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773 and also due to negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answer the Issue No.1 Partly in the Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner claiming the compensation amount of Rs.5,00,000/- with respect to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

The petitioner produced wound certificate issued by Silicon City Hospital, Hosakote, Bangalore and discharge MVC.6376/2022 summary issued by Raksha Multispeciality Hospital, Bangalore and prayed to award compensation amount.
The respondents not disputed the said documents.
On perusal of Ex.P.6 the wound certificate, it discloses that the petitioner has sustained severe neck pain.
The doctor opined that the above said injury is simple in nature.

Therefore, taking all these facts and nature of injury, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.20,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.

Shobha.V vs K.S.R.T.C on 27 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3322775/
5 21.
The petitioner produced medical bills which is marked as Ex.P.11.
The respondents not denied the medical bills.

On perusal of the said medical bills and also considering the bills and also treatment taken by the petitioner in the hospital, the petitioner is entitled to claim the medical bills amount of Rs.7,920/- under the head of medical expenditure.
22. The petitioner not produced any documents with respect to expenditure of transportation, food and other charges.
However, the petitioner produced discharge summary issued by Raksha Multispeciality Hospital, Bangalore which is marked as Ex.P.8.
It discloses that, the petitioner took treatment inpatient in the said MVC.6376/2022 hospital from 04-10-2022 to 06-10-2022 for about 03 days.

Therefore, considering the treatment taken as inpatient in the hospital, this tribunal has award reasonable compensation of Rs.3,000/- under the head transportation, nourishment and conveyance charges.
23. To prove the disability, neither the petitioner had examined her treated Doctor, nor produced any disability certificate.
Hence the petitioner is not entitled to claim any compensation amount under the head loss of income on account of permanent disability and also under the head future medical expenses.

24. The petitioner stated that, prior to the accident he was hale, healthy and aged about 33 years,
she was working as Housewife and due to injuries sustained in the accident, she is unable to attend his work and lost her earnings.
The petitioner had not produced any documents to prove her income and avocation.
This accident occurred in the year 2022.

However by considering the age and nature of injury sustained by the petitioner, this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation amount of Rs.15,000/- under the head loss of income during laid up period.
The petitioner was working as housewife and due to accidental injuries her routine work was hampered for some days.

Therefore, by considering this aspect and the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal awarded the amount of Rs.20,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of loss of amenities.

26. Considering the oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:
 Under the Heads Amount 1. Pain and Sufferings Rs. 20,000/-
2. Medical Expenses Rs. 7,920/-
3. Transportation, Nourishment, 3,000/-

4. Loss of Income during Laid-up Rs. 15,000/-

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.65,920/- which is rounded of to Rs.66,000/-.

27. Interest:
MVC.6376/2022

For awarding interest, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest can be awarded in MVC Cases, cannot be more than 6% p.a.

Hence, I am of the opinion that,
the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
28. Liability:-
The respondent No.1 is the RC owner-cum-Insurer of KSRTC bus bearing Reg No.KA-57/F-3773.

Respondent No.2 is the RC owner and Respondent No.3 is the i n s u r e d a n d r e s p o n d e n t N o . 4 i s t h e i n s u r e r o f t h e L o r r y b e a r i n g Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498.
29.

As already discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus driver and also due to negligent parking of Lorry by it's driver on the road.
Hence, the respondent No.1 and 4 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further, the counsel for the respondent No.1 filed memo by admitting the 50% of the liability and counsel for respondent No.4 has also admitted liability to the extent of 50%.

Hence, the Respondent No.1 being RC Owner-cum-Insurer of the KSRTC Bus and MVC.6376/2022 Respondent No.4 being Insurer of the Lorry are primarily held liable to pay the 50% each of the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.

30. The respondent No.1 took contention that, already the interim compensation amount of Rs.31,670/- towards medical expenses has been paid to the petitioner and that would be deducted from the liability amount of respondent No.1.

Therefore, out of the liability of respondent No.1 the interim compensation paid by the KSRTC should be deducted, which comes as follows:
Rs.66,000/- - 50% - Rs.31,670/- = Rs.1,330/-.
Hence, respondent No.1 is liable to pay Rs.1,330/- with accrued interest.
The remaining 50% of liability i.e., Rs.33,000/- should be paid by the respondent No.4 with accrued interest.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answered Issue No.2 in the Partly Affirmative.

Issue No.3:

For the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER

The claim petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost as hereunder:
MVC.6376/2022
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.34,330/- with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.

The respondent No.1 being RC Owner-cum- Insurer of the KSRTC Bus is liable to pay of Rs.1,330/- & respondent No.4 being the insurer of the Lorry is liable to pay Rs.33,000/- to the petitioner and they are directed to deposit the entire compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner with proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
